title: Basie's big band breaks up in 1950
summary: The big band folded as dance halls declined, and Basie formed a small group with Clark Terry and Serge Chaloff.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, when you -- at the end of these 12 years or whatever, with Basie, why did you --
Oh, you left when the big band broke up?

Yeah, the band broke up in 1950 because that's when the little bands began to take over. And the dance halls, they began to diminish. And people, they didn't dance anymore. It became like more of a concert thing when you played, you know. In the smaller clubs, you would just -- they would sit and drink, you know. It was nightclub instead of dance hall, then. And 1950, Basie got a small band together, you remember, it was Serge Chaloff and Clark Terry.
Clark had been in the band.
Yes, he had been in the big band. Yeah. We had Snooky Young, Clark Terry, myself and Emmett Berry.
That was a good trumpet section.
